title: Sub-cycle metrology of bright quantum light
authors: Shima Gholam-Mirzaei, Michael T. Weil, David N. Purschke, Katarzyna M. Kowalczyk, André Staudte, David M. Villeneuve, Paul B. Corkum, Jeff S. Lundeen, T. J. Hammond, Giulio Vampa
abstract: In quantum optics, quantization of the electromagnetic field typically occurs in a finite volume - a cavity - which results in discrete frequency modes where photons are created, annihilated and exchanged between such modes. As a result, evolution of quantum optical states is periodic in the carrier wave of the field, measurement protocols return cycle-averaged information, and any sub-cycle evolution that is foundational to many light-matter interactions, especially at high field strengths, remains hidden. Adapting an attosecond technique, here we capture the electric-field evolution of a quantum optical state, femtosecond bright squeezed vacuum, with sub-cycle precision. We find that it consists of many stochastic, time-localized bursts within each pump pulse whose phase randomly switches between two values. We exploit the random phase flips to generate quantum random bit sequences with a generation rate that can reach petahertz frequencies. In addition, the sub-cycle resolution allows us to measure coherence functions of the waveforms between any two times, which we explain with a superposition of time-limited modes. These results bridge attosecond metrology and quantum optics and pave the way to measuring quantum light-matter interactions as they evolve on a few-femtosecond time scale, and integrate quantum randomness in petahertz electronics.
summary: The research overcomes the limitation of cycle-averaging in quantum light measurements by employing sub-cycle resolution metrology on bright squeezed vacuum. This technique reveals that the quantum state consists of stochastic, time-localized bursts whose relative phases are randomly distributed between two values separated by $\pi$. These random phase flips are then harnessed to generate high-rate quantum random number sequences approaching petahertz frequencies.
main_problem: To measure the electric-field evolution of quantum light (femtosecond bright squeezed vacuum) with sub-cycle precision, overcoming limitations where conventional measurements average over multiple field cycles.
main_result: The study successfully characterized stochastic, time-localized bursts in the BSV and demonstrated that the random phase flips between adjacent bursts can be exploited to generate quantum random bit sequences at petahertz frequencies.
method: Attosecond metrology techniques are adapted using nonlinear absorption on a silicon CMOS sensor to map the electric field $E(t)$ with sub-cycle resolution, followed by statistical analysis of phase differences.
model_or_system: The system uses Bright Squeezed Vacuum (BSV) generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. The temporal structure is modeled using Whittaker–Shannon time-limited modes, which are localized in time and distinct from conventional Schmidt modes.
key_observables: Time-resolved coherence functions ($g^{(1)}(t_1, t_2)$, $g^{(2)}(t_1, t_2)$), burst statistics (number, duration), and the bimodal distribution of relative phase differences ($\Delta\phi$).
important_parameters: Sub-cycle precision; petahertz generation rates; femtosecond burst widths ($\sim 17$ fs); $\pi$-separated phases.
main_assumptions: The random phase flips are assumed to reflect spontaneous symmetry breaking, and the analysis relies on fitting procedures derived from theoretical models of joint spectral amplitudes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate experimental setups (Fig. 1a), pulse energy/signal histograms (Figs. 1b, 1c), representative burst waveforms (Fig. 1d), coherence function measurements (Fig. 4a/c), and the final NIST test results for randomness (Fig. S10).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from describing the fundamental limitation of cycle-averaged quantum optics to detailing the experimental measurement technique, characterizing the stochastic burst structure, and finally demonstrating the application of phase randomness for high-rate QRNG.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges advanced quantum optics metrology (attosecond techniques) with quantum information processing by providing a physical mechanism to generate certified random numbers at extremely high bandwidths.
